annie-rodwell-1920-08-11.A1:
HOLD WHITE MAN AND COLORED WOMAN ON MANN ACT
Pittsburg, Pa., Aug. 18—N. L. Starling, white, and Mrs. Annie Rodwell, colored, are detained in jail in this city fighting extradition, instituted by the State of Georgia, their former home. The strange story told of how white men of the south separate colored men from their wives was set up in the bill of particulars. Mrs. Rodwell formerly lived at Valdosta, Ga., and was separated from her husband by Starling, said to be the son of a wealthy farmer.

annie-rodwell-1920-08-11.A2:
STRANGEST CASE IN HISTORY OF SOUTH ATTRACTS ATTENTION
(Special to the Tribune)
Pittsburg, Pa., Aug. 25.—The state of Georgia is making desperate efforts to secure the extradition of N. N. Starling, white, and Mrs. Annie Rodwell, colored, both of whom are in the local jail. The case is the strangest that has ever come to light in the history of the local courts and again shows up racial relations in the South in their true light.

Both the man and woman are married and had their home in Hahira, Ga., where Starling's father is a wealthy lumberman. Mrs. Rodwell's husband works on the Starling plantation.

Two years ago the younger Starling saw pretty Mrs. Rodwell for the first time and fell in love with her. The elder Starling noticed the intimacy and organized a party of lynchers to take the woman away. On the way to the Rodwell house, young Starling met them and succeeded in getting them to turn back by saying the house was filled with armed colored people and they would all be killed. Frightened, Mrs. Rodwell left the Starling farm and went to live in Valdosta, Ga., fourteen miles away.

Although Starling knew his father and brothers would lynch the colored girl if he kept paying attentions to her, he continued to visit her house, and two weeks ago was caught there by his family. Another lynching party was organized, of which Starling learned just in time to get the girl in his automobile and drive twelve miles to a nearby swamp, where they spent the night in water up to their knees hiding from the mob. They succeeded in getting to the train and came to Pittsburg.

Now the state of Georgia wants the couple returned. Starling says he is perfectly willing to go without extradition papers, but he knows if his soulmate goes back, she will be lynched.

champion-jones-1920-07-31.A1:
TELLS STRANGE STORY
Negro Says He Was Whipped on Way to Jail.
Florence, Aug. 2.—Hampton Jones, a negro brought here early Sunday morning by Constable Rose, of Pamlico, and lodged in the county jail on the charge of assault and battery with intent to kill, claims that he was taken away from the constable on their way here Saturday night, by six or eight masked white men and severely whipped. The negro claims that while passing through a swamp near Pamlico, the car in which the driver, the constable and he were riding, was stopped by the men who demanded of the constable the prisoner; that the constable protested, but that he was taken away from the officer and carried out in the woods a short distance and severely whipped by the men, who were white, he says;but he was unable to identify them. The negro was examined after reaching the county jail by a Florence physician and no signs of a whipping were found on his body, the only wound of any kind being a severe cut in his head
champion-jones-1920-07-31.A2:
which the arresting officer found necessary to make when arresting the negro Saturday night, when the negro not only resisted arrest but throwing the officer down was getting the best of him until a white man came to his rescue and in the fight the officer used his club effectively.

The constable states that in the swamp where the negro alleges the whipping took place that several men did attempt to stop the car but shoving them off and speeding up he was able to get away and land his prisoner safely in jail. He took the men to be negroes and he thought them to be friends of the prisoner who was attempting to free the prisoner.

The negro was arrested on the charge of assault and battery with intent to kill, having cut another negro at a frolic at Pamplico Saturday night. The negro he cut is not seriously hurt.

john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A2:
MOB RIDDLES NEGRO ACCUSED OF ATTACK Prisoner Taken From Sheriff and Deputies.
GRAHAM, N. C., Aug. 25.—Accused of attempting an attack on a four-year-old girl, John Jeffress, a negro, was shot to death near here to-day by a mob of about fifty men. The mob overpowered Sheriff Story and six deputies as they were transferring the negro from the county jail, where he was placed after his arrest early to-day, to the court house for preliminary hearing.

Jeffress was taken by the mob about a mile and a half outside of Graham and his body riddled with bullets. Sheriff Story said to-night that neither he nor his deputies recognized any of the leaders of the mob and that the negro was given up after a brief scuffle and after the officers realized that resistance would be useless.

The alleged attempt to attack the child took place early to-day near the little girl's home. Cries of her mother were said to have frightened the negro away before the child was harmed.

RUSSIAN PEOPLE WOULD STOP STRIFE
By the Associated Press.

Sebastopol, Crimea, Aug. 26.—Civil war in Russia would cease immediately if the Russian people were free to organize the government according to their own wishes. General Baron Wrangel, who was recognized by France a few days ago, declared here today.

They are not able to do this at present, however, because of the domination of the soviet leaders and the fight must go on until Russians are free to take matters in their own hands, he continued.

NEGRO IS LYNCHED
FOR USUAL CRIME

Durham, Aug. 26.—One the spot where James Ray was killed during a battle between Durham machine gunners guarding the Alamance county jail on the night of July 19 and a masked mob, an unmasked mob yesterday, after overpowered Sheriff C. D. Story and seven other officers having John Jeffress, a negro prisoner charged with assaulting a four-year-old white girl, at her home near Elon college, and putting him in an automobile rushed him to a point between Graham and Burlington, where they riddled his body with bullets.

The crime for which the negro was arrested occurred festerday morning about 10 o'clock. The little girl, Mary Rudd, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. A. L Rudd, had started from the house to a field where her father was at work. The negro, it is said, grabbed her near the house and carried her bodily to a nearby pasture where it is alleged he attempted criminal as sault. The child cried and the mother heard her cry, and screamed, and the negro ran.

The alarm was given immediately and soon an armed posses was hunting for the negro. Sheriff Story was notified and he immediately formed a posse. The officers trailed him to the Graham railway station and found him hiding in honeysuckle vines near the station. He submitted to arrest meekly and after being placed in the Alamance jail is said by Sheric Story to have admitted the crime.

It is court week in Graham and several hundred citizens were gathered around the jail and courthouse. They learned that the officers were to take the negro to the courtroom for trial at 3 o'clock yesterday afternoon and as the official party with the prisoner left the jail a mob, said by the sheriff to have been composed of between 25 and 50 men, crowded around the party. There was a sudden surge forward, and in the twinkling of an eye the negro had been taken from the officers, placed in an automobile and rushed away.

The attack on the officers was something of a surprise and happened so quickly that neither members of the mob or the officers drew their pistols. The officers made no attempt to follow the mob. Sheriff Story said over long distance telephone tonight that he had not visited the scene where Jeffress was put to death and did not know whether a coroner's inquest had been held.
john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A4:
NEGRO LYNCHED IN NORTH CAROLINA
ADMITS CRIME AND PAYS PENALTY AT HANDS OF A SMALL MOB.
Durham, N. C., Aug. 25.—On almost the identical spot where James Ray fell mortally wounded during the battle between a masked mob and the Durham machine gun company guarding the Alamance county jail on the night of July 19, another mob this afternoon overpowered Sheriff C. D. Story and six deputies and took away from them John Jeffress, a negro charged with assaulting a four-year-old child.

Afterwards the mob carried the negro without resistance to a lonely spot halfway between Burlington and Belmont cotton mills, west of Graham, and riddled his body with bullets. He wes reported to Sheriff Story afterwards as dead.

The crime for which the young negro was put to death is alleged to have been committed at 10 o'clock this morning near the child's home. Cries of her mother, it is said, caused the negro to run, leaving the little girl without serious injury.

An armed posse formed immediately after the crime was reported, but it was Sheriff Story's posse, composed of deputy sheriffs and police officers of both Graham and Burlington, that landed the prisoner. They found him crouched in a honeysuckle vine near the Graham railroad station. He was arrested and placed in the Alamance county jail shortly after the noon hour. He admitted the crime, Sheriff Story said.
At 3 o'clock this afternoon Sheriff Story and his six assistants started with Jeffress to the courthouse one block away. Arriving at the spot where Ray was killed, a mob formed around the officers and their prisoner. There was a sudden surge forward and in the twinkling of an eye, according to the sheriff, the prisoner had been taken from the officer and was placed in an automobile and rushed away.
john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A11:
OVERPOWER SHERIFF
THEN LYNCH NEGRO
BURLINGTON, N. C., Aug. 26 (United Press.)—John Jeffries, 18 year old Negro, was lynched one mile from Graham late yesterday afternoon for ann assault upon Mary Lee Rudd, six-year-old white girl, near Elon College yesterday morning as she was carrying water to her father working in a field near the house.

The sheriff and seven deputies were overpowered near the jal by a mob of eight masked men as he was taking the prisoner to court for trial, the court being in session and a true bill had been found.

It is said the Negro confessed. When found by the coroner twenty bullet holes were found in his body.

john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A20:
MEMBER OF THE ASSOCIATED MICRO PRESS FIRST IN SERVICE
Editorials.

SATURDAY SEPTEMBER 4, 1920

There were no National Guardsmen at Graham on the 25th of August, the civil authorities failed utterly and Graham finally succeeded in disgraving itself and in particular in disguising himself, generally—it had to have its lynching.

A little more than a month ago a company of the National Guard were ordered to Graham to prevent a lynching, and found it necessary to fire on the crowd that attempted to take the law into their own hands, killing one and wounding two. The citizens of Graham became very indignant over the "wanton killing" of peaceful citizens? by the Guardsmen, and avowed themselves as lovers of law and order. The Guardsmen are removed. Court is in session. The grand jury returns a "true bill" Judge Allen is on the bench, announces that court is ready to try John Jeffress for rape and orders the sheriff to bring the prisoner into court. The Sheriff and "his deputies" retired to the jail a hundred yards away to get the prisoner, the way back "a thousand city citizens" as a flash overpowered the sheriff and his assistants" the Negro is whirled away in a big automobile, shot to death and in less than twenty minutes a thousand people had viewed the body. All afternoon people drove out to see the "SIGHT" among others "MANY LADIES" and thus Graham's lust for blood is satisfied. Thus ends the tale.
john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A21:
Also discovers That Jeffers was Taken From Sheriff By Unknown Persons
Burlington, Sept. / 1—At the close of court last week the grand jury came to two important decisions. It was the duty of this body to investigate the recent killings in Alamance county. In doing so it found that James Ray came to his death by gun shots from the machine gunners, that there was no mob at the jail and that there was no provocation for the killing of Ray. The other decision affected the recent lynching of the Negro, John Jeffers. The jury found that the Negro was taken from the hands of the officers by unknown persons and shot, and that the sheriff and officers had done all they could to protect the Negro. There is something essentially wrong with Alamance's sense of duty or Fair Play.
john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A24:
SHERIFF TURNS OVER PRISONER
DURHAM, N. C, Sept. I.-Sheriff C. B. Storey and six deputies, while in a lonely spot near Burlington and Graham, turned their prisoner. John Jeffries, over to a mob of 150 men, who shot him to death for alleged assault upon a 4-year-old white girl. The assault is said to have consisted of Jeffries' speaking to the little girl as he passed the house. She went back and told her mother that a strange colored man had spoken to her. The mother gave the alarm; the mob gathered. In the meantime Jeffries had been arrested by the sheriff, who apparently conveniently traveled the same path as the mob, and the victim was executed according to the "laws of the South."
john-jeffress-graham-1920-08-25.A26:
NATIONAL WOMAN'S COUNCIL OF C. M. E. CHURCH MEETS
Frivolous Charge Produced to Give Mob Chance to Get Revenge For Former Failure.

Sheriff Storey was well aware of the plans of the mob and realized the mob was marching on the fall when he opened the door of the jail, marched to the courthouse several blocks away. The story as given by Sheriff Storey is as follows:
"At three o'clock this afternoon, my six assistants and myself, started with Jeffries to the courthouse one block away. A mob formed around us and the prisoner. There was a sudden surge forward and in the twinkling of an eye, the prisoner had been taken from us and placed in an automobile and rushed away."
"There was not a shot fired, not even a gun drawn during the minute scuffle between the mob and officers," Sheriff Storey said tonight that resistance would have been folly as the mob was made up of between 25 and 50 determined men. There were at least 160 additional men nearby whose sympathies were with the mob, he stated tonight. He said he did not know anyone in the mob.
The lynching occurred on almost the identical spot where James Ray fell mortally wounded during the battle between a masked mob and the Durham machine gun company guarding the Alamance county jail on the night of July 19.

leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A1:
Insulted White Girls—Shot.
Danville, Va., Aug. 26.—An unidentified negro charged with having insulted two white girls here yesterday was shot today at Virgilia after having been tracked to that place by a posse with bloodhounds. Before being killed by Marse Elam, a member of the posse, he wounded one of his pursuers when he opened fire on them.
leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A8:
POSSE KILLS NEGRO WHO
SHOT DOWN HALIFAX MAN
Leslie Allen, of Alabama, Pays With Life for Wounding James Baptist.

INSULTS TWO WHITE GIRLS

Bloodhounds Trailed Negro to Farm House Near Virgilina—His Body Riddled as He Lay Hidden in Bed Quilts.
DANVILLE, VA., August 26.—Leslie Allen, 22, a negro from Alabama, but recently a resident of Petersburg, was shot to death by an armed posse this morning at 9:30 o'clock near Virgillina.

He paid with his life for shooting and wounding James Baptist, a wealthy Halifax Courier at Buffalo Lithia Station yesterday, after the white man had to arrest the negro for an insult to two little white girls on the hotel property. Baptist is in Halcyon Hospital at South Boston, where he was taken in an automobile and is said today that he would recover as the revolver bullet which entered the chest had been deflected by a rib and had not punctured the lung.

Allen, before being shot to pieces, shot and wounded Mason Elam, brother-in-law of Baptist, after he had been cornered in a negro hut two miles from Virgillina, in Mecklenburg County. The remains were taken back to Buffalo and turned over to the sheriff.

Cursed Girls in Hotel.

Allen was employed two weeks ago as a porter at the Buffalo Hotel and had previously been a chauffeur for a man named Parham at Petersburg Yesterday evening two little girls who set up ten pins on the hotel grounds were closing up the alley when the negro appeared, they alleged, and demanded that they set the pins as he wanted to roll. When they told him that only white patrons had the privilege, he is said to have addressed highly objectionable remarks and to have cursed the white race.

One of the girls reported the mat
leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A9:
POSSE KILLS NEGRO WHO SHOT DOWN HALIFAX MAN
ter to Baptist, who took a few friends with the purpose of apprehending the negro. Alien was located at Buffalo station before dark. No sooner had the small party of men appeared when Allen drew two large army Colt revolvers and poured the contents of both magazines, eighteen shots in all, at them. Only one bullet was effective, this striking Baptist in the chest. None of the white men were armed, and while they scurried for shooting irons Allen got away. A posse was formed and bloodhounds secured and throughout the night the brush was combed, but with no avail.

Amos Organized Posse.

It was R. E. Amos, a merchant at Virgilina, who brought about the negro's discovery. At 5 this morning a strange negro was found by him loitering at his store. Restive and ill at ease he aroused the merchant's suspicions, especially when he said that he had been employed at Buffalo Hotel. He gave his name as "John Brown," and made away hastily. Amos called him back and he came, but realizing that he might be in error and having no revolver, Amos let the man go. Amos then turned to the telephone, got in touch with the police at South Boston and soon learned that there could not be any mistake.

The suspect wore a green cap and leggings, which was the description given by the Halifax authorities. Amos then used the wire freely and got word to the posse and other farmers, who were placed at convenient points for the purpose of hemining the negro in a given area.

Killed Victim in Bed.

The posse arrived from Buffalo, twelve miles distant, in a short while and a definite trail was established, this leading to the two-story frame house of George Burrell, a negro tenant of L. G. Chandler. The house was surrounded and the lower floor searched without avail. Ten men heavily armed went upstairs and in one room saw an object wrapped up in blankets and bed covers, on the top of which were bandboxes and other debris, spread in careless confusion.

One of the men was just about to prod the object with his gun barrel when a shot rang out, and Mason Elam went to his knees, shot in the foot. In a second the ten men opened fire and poured several volleys into the writhing bed quilts, ceasing only when the object lay still. Then they uncovered it and found Allen, his head virtually shot from his trunk.

The posse members said that they had made no mistake as there were all the distinguishing marks on the guilty negro and his two Colt revolvers with empty magazines. The posse had a warrant for the arrest of the negro and there is no doubt that it was he, under camouflage, fired the one shot at Elam.
leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A11:
ALABAMA NEGRO IS SUMMARILY LYNCHED (Associated Press)
DANVILLE, VA., Aug. 26—Leslie Allen, negro native of Alabama, was shot and killed in a negro shanty at Virgilia, near here today by a posse which was pursuing him for an alleged insult to two white girls employed at the hotel at Buffalo Springs, Va.

During a running fight with the negroe, james Baptist, posseman, was shot and seriously wounded by the fugitive who then escaped. Bloodhounds tracked the negro to the house where he was barricaded on the second floor and kept up a continuous fire until his head was nearly blown off by a discharge from a shot gun.
leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A12:
NEGRO KILLED
FIGHTING POSSE
Virginian's Slayer Wounds Pursuers Before Meeting Death.
(By United Press.)

Danville, Va., Aug. 26.—A negro who shot and wounded James Baptist was cornered and shot to death in a camp near here today, according to word brought back from a posse which pursued the man. Before the negro was killed he wounded a member of the posse.

The shooting of Baptist, a wealthy resident of Halifax County, occurred at Buffalo Lithia Springs. It was said the unidentified man wanted to play tenpins but the girls employed to set up the pins demurred.

Baptist and a party of men pursued the man off the property after which he is alleged to have turned and fired twenty shots. Baptist was the only one wounded.
leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A15:
KILL NEGRO.
VIRGILIANA, Virginia, Aug. 25.
—Lesslie Allen, a negro was shot and killed near here Thursday by a posse of Halifax county citizens, following charges that Allen had insulted two white girls at Buffalo Springs, Va.
leslie-allen-virgilina-1920-08-25.A16:
VIRGINIA GOVERNOR TO PROBE NEGRO LYNCHING
NORFOLK, Va., Aug. 28.—The killing of an unidentified negro near Norfolk Wednesday night by a posse of 300 men will be investigated by Governor Davis, it was announced today.

The negro is alleged to have insulted two white girls at a local hotel. He shot John Baptiste, a white man who resented his advances to the girls, and later the negro wounded two members of the posse.

Bloodhounds trailed him several miles out of Norfolk, locating him in a thicket where he was put to death.
